identification.summary: Scarab is a suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor first documented publicly by Symantec in January 2015, which described highly targeted attacks against Russian-speaking people since at least January 2012 using a custom backdoor called Scieron [S1][S2]. SentinelLabs later assessed with high confidence that CERT-UA's UAC-0026 is Scarab, based on malware design, associated loaders and reuse of actor-unique infrastructure [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Symantec: attacks dating to at least January 2012; reported January 2015 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: Vendor/agency names: Scarab (Symantec, SentinelLabs); UAC-0026 (CERT-UA) assessed by SentinelLabs to be Scarab [S3][S5]. No Microsoft Typhoon/Storm name is recorded in this encyclopedia for this actor. Malware names Scieron and HeaderTip are tools, not actor names [S3].

attribution.confidence: SentinelLabs assessed with moderate confidence that Scarab is Chinese speaking and operates for geopolitical intelligence collection, and with high confidence that UAC-0026 is Scarab [S3].
attribution.basis: SentinelLabs cites targets since 2020 including Ukraine in March 2022, specific language use, and lure documents created on Windows systems with Chinese language settings [S3]. The UAC-0026 link rests on malware design, loaders and reused infrastructure [S3]. No government attribution to a named PRC organization was found in the sources gathered.

objectives: SentinelLabs assesses geopolitical intelligence collection [S3]; specific objectives are not publicly established.

regions: Russia and the United States (individuals, per Symantec-derived reporting) [S2][S6]
Syria listed by ETDA, without detail [S6]
targeting.notes: Symantec described attacks on a small number of individuals, typically against Russian speakers, fewer than ten machines infected per month on average [S1][S2]. The 2022 lure mimicked the National Police of Ukraine and concerned preserving video evidence of Russian military crimes [S5]. SentinelLabs called it the first public example of a Chinese threat actor targeting Ukraine since the invasion began [S5].

capabilities.summary: Custom backdoor Scieron (and the more capable Scieron.B, which can hide a TCP port in communications) used from at least 2012 [S1][S2]. By 2022 the actor used phishing with relevant lures delivering a RAR archive with an executable that opens a decoy document and drops the DLL HeaderTip (officecleaner.dat) plus a batch file [S5]. HeaderTip is a small 32-bit C++ DLL acting as a first-stage downloader for later modules; SentinelLabs says Scieron may be its predecessor [S3].

diamond.adversary: Suspected Chinese-speaking espionage actor; sponsor not publicly identified [S3].

diamond.socioPolitical: Geopolitical intelligence collection, with the 2022 lure exploiting the Russia-Ukraine war [S3].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints reached by email with archive attachments and DLL execution [S5].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1-2: Low-volume, individual-focused espionage means key terrain is personal and organizational email and endpoints of people with Russia-Ukraine regional involvement [S2]. STEP 3: Template is a themed phishing lure, then RAR with executable, then DLL and batch drop, then HeaderTip downloading later modules [S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued small-scale collection of regional geopolitical information [S3]. MDCOA is use of the same lures against coalition or allied personnel during a crisis (assumption beyond sources). Candidate indicators: RAR attachments with executables opening decoy documents, files named officecleaner.dat, and the CERT-UA IOCs [S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Share CERT-UA and SentinelLabs indicators into situational awareness feeds [S5]. (2) Email-borne, individual-targeted activity requires coordination with partner CERTs and allied intelligence rather than only network defense. (3) Confidence in actor identity is vendor-level only [S3]; avoid treating it as government attribution. (4) Mission assurance: protect personnel with Eastern Europe portfolios from themed lures.

provenance.importedSummary: Scarab APT was first spotted in 2015, but is believed to have been active since at least 2012, conducting surgical attacks against a small number of individuals across the world, including Russia and the United States. The backdoor deployed by Scarab in their campaigns is most commonly known as Scieron.
